LESSON: JOSEPH INTERPRETS A DREAM

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Holy Bible
Topic 2.5: Joseph interprets a Dream

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Joseph interprets a Dream. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How was Joseph able to interpret dreams?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. retell the story of Joseph interpreting a dream
2. apply lessons learnt by depending on God’s wisdom
3. recognise that, ‘the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.’

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: JOSEPH INTERPRETS A DREAM
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Joseph interprets a Dream helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: JOSEPH INTERPRETS A DREAM
Study Joseph interprets a Dream like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Retell the story of Joseph interpreting a dream

What this means
In this part you learn to retell the story of Joseph interpreting a dream. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: retell the story of Joseph interpreting a dream.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Joseph interprets a Dream” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can retell the story of Joseph interpreting a dream. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply lessons learnt by depending on God’s wisdom

What this means
In this part you learn to apply lessons learnt by depending on God’s wisdom. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply lessons learnt by depending on God’s wisdom.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Joseph interprets a Dream in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply lessons learnt by depending on God’s wisdom. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Recognise that, ‘the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.’

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise that, ‘the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.’. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise that, ‘the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.’.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise that, ‘the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.’. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Joseph interprets a Dream is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Joseph interprets a Dream” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: retell the story of Joseph interpreting a dream)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Joseph interprets a Dream in your own words. (skill: apply lessons learnt by depending on God’s wisdom)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: recognise that, ‘the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.’)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Joseph interprets a Dream to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: retell the story of Joseph interpreting a dream.
3. Practise this skill: apply lessons learnt by depending on God’s wisdom.
4. Practise this skill: recognise that, ‘the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.’.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Joseph interprets a Dream from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Joseph interprets a Dream: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Joseph interprets a Dream?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How was Joseph able to interpret dreams?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Joseph interprets a Dream means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: retell the story of Joseph interpreting a dream.
5. Be able to: apply lessons learnt by depending on God’s wisdom.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
